page: Microsoft Azure D64ns_v6 is a network-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Dnv6 server family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. It is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. This virtual machine runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark data indicates strong performance in several areas. The processor demonstrates high efficiency in extended instructions, encryption, and physics calculations, as evidenced by top-quartile PassMark CPU scores. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and Redis SET operations also rank in the top 25 percent, with Redis achieving 71.06 million operations per second. Small-block cached memory bandwidth is highly efficient at 4125.39 GB/sec, though large-block uncached read and write bandwidths perform in the average range. Notably, PassMark memory scores fall into the lower 25 percent tier. The CPU includes Advanced Matrix Extensions and AVX-512, which contribute to strong prompt processing speeds during LLM inference across small, medium, and large models.

In terms of resource configuration, the D64ns_v6 does not include any local NVMe or SSD storage, requiring reliance on external Premium Storage options. This design prioritizes network throughput and compute density over local data persistence. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers high compute density and strong cryptographic and database processing capabilities per resource unit, though workloads requiring high-speed local scratch space or top-tier memory performance may face bottlenecks due to the lack of local disks and lower memory benchmark scores.

This server configuration is appropriate for network-heavy workloads, database operations, static web serving, and multi-threaded decompression tasks. The inclusion of AMX and AVX-512 instructions also makes it capable of handling CPU-based LLM inference and vector-heavy mathematical computations.
